prompt: CREATE A NEW COPYRIGHT-SAFE ANATOMY-LED PALEOART SCENE, using reference 1 only for its unusual portrait spatial design and reference 2 for Velociraptor feather/anatomy cues. Portrait 2:3 composition. Exact animal count is mandatory: FOUR juvenile Protoceratops and ONE Velociraptor mongoliensis, no other animals. Place the four small juvenile Protoceratops as a loose asymmetrical broken crescent across the lower half, at four different depths and orientations, with clear space between every body, full tails and all four limbs visible where perspective allows. They are calmly foraging/walking, not forming a defensive ring. Place the single Velociraptor alone in the upper-left FAR MIDGROUND, clearly separated but large enough to identify, roughly 18–22 percent of image width. It walks left in crisp side profile and does not look at the juveniles: fully feathered compact body, wing-like feathered forelimbs held close, low narrow head, long stiff feathered tail, two long legs, one subtle raised second toe. Preserve a broad empty S-shaped visual corridor from lower center to upper right, a low-to-moderate ground-level camera, deep landscape layers, and large quiet sky. No centered lineup, no mirrored poses, no eye-line confrontation, no chase, no attack, no blood, no adult Protoceratops, no nest, no parenting, no text or border. Naturalistic museum-grade digital paleoart with restrained colors.
